analysis.title: Search under siege? Alphabet, OpenAI and the battle for the world's most valuable ad auction
key_insights: Alphabet Q3 2026 revenue grew 25% y/y to USD 127.6bn, the fastest pace since 2021, led by Google Cloud, which more than doubled to USD 30.7bn on AI infrastructure demand and TPU system sales. Operating income rose 30% and the Gemini app passed one billion users.

Google Search & other revenue rose 12% to USD 63.4bn, below consensus of about USD 65.0bn and down from 17-19% growth in the previous three quarters. Search was 49.7% of total revenue, below half for the first time in this cycle.

Total advertising rose 11% to USD 82.0bn, also below forecasts. EPS was USD 2.12, reduced by an USD 8.7bn loss on equity holdings. Free cash flow was negative USD 9.1bn, including a USD 5.2bn payment for a 2018 EU fine, with quarterly capex of USD 51.4bn. Shares fell more than 9% after hours.
Management says query growth, including commercial queries, is the highest in five years, while Search revenue growth slowed. The report reads this as lower revenue per query.

Explanations for the slowdown: AI-generated answers are harder to monetise than ten blue links, tougher comparisons after a strong 2025, and advertisers testing new AI surfaces with part of budgets that previously went to Google's auction. These are not mutually exclusive.

Management attributed the step-down versus Q2 mainly to FX, APAC retailers hit by the end of the EU de minimis exemption, and a Q2 boosted by the World Cup. The authors say FX was only a slight y/y headwind and does not explain most of the step-down. Search revenue was flat q/q against a 4% rise a year earlier, and Schindler conceded AI Mode grows fast but monetises less well.

OpenAI began US ad tests on 9 February 2026 for logged-in adults on the Free and Go tiers. Plus, Pro, Business and Enterprise users remain ad-free. Early ads sold at CPMs of about USD 60 with USD 200,000-300,000 minimum commitments. Cost-per-click bidding and a self-serve Ads Manager arrived by April.

ChatGPT Ads reached a USD 1bn annualised run rate on 31 August, under 200 days after launch. On 21 October ads expanded to 26 more countries (89 total), with more than 100,000 advertisers having run campaigns. OpenAI targets USD 2.5bn of ad revenue in 2026. Shopify and Etsy partnerships allow checkout inside ChatGPT.

Scale gap: Google Search generates about 60 times OpenAI's annualised ad run rate in one quarter. Ads are about 2.5% of OpenAI revenue, agencies have questioned performance, reporting is aggregate-only, and a run rate is not booked revenue. The report argues a few points of commercial search budget moving to conversational ads would still be material for Alphabet.

Evidence of a mass exodus from Google is limited. Google handles about 90% of conventional searches per StatCounter, and ChatGPT was about 0.24% of combined Google-plus-ChatGPT referral traffic in August 2026. ChatGPT claims 1.2bn weekly users and Meta AI reached about one billion monthly users by mid-2025.

Funding: trailing-twelve-month capex reached USD 160bn and free cash flow was negative for two consecutive quarters, about USD 3.9bn negative in Q3 excluding the EU fine. Capital-light Search profit is being replaced by capital-intensive Cloud profit, which lowers return on capital.

Alphabet owns chips (TPUs), cloud, models and distribution, which the report calls a full-stack hedge that lets it serve AI answers more cheaply and capture AI demand whichever company wins the interface.

Items to monitor: paid clicks versus cost-per-click in the 10-Q, disclosure on AI Mode monetisation, OpenAI's booked ad revenue ahead of its planned listing, and advertiser budget allocation between the two platforms.

market_movers.rationale: Search growth slowed to 12% and missed consensus of about USD 65.0bn, while OpenAI is building a competing ad business. Shares fell more than 9% after hours. The note gives no rating or price target.

earnings_insights: Alphabet Q3 2026 (reported 28 October 2026): revenue USD 127.6bn, +25% y/y (+24.6% per Table 1).
Google Search & other: reported USD 63.4bn (+12.0% y/y), vs consensus est about USD 65.0bn (LSEG via CNBC).
Total Google advertising: reported USD 82.0bn (+10.6% y/y), below forecasts. YouTube ads reported USD 11.2bn (+9.2%), Google Network USD 7.5bn (+1.4%).
Google Cloud: reported USD 30.7bn (+102.6% y/y) vs USD 15.2bn in Q3 2025. Subscriptions, platforms & devices: USD 14.3bn (+11.0%).
EPS reported USD 2.12, described as a miss and reduced by an USD 8.7bn loss on equity holdings. No consensus EPS figure is given.
Free cash flow reported negative USD 9.1bn including a USD 5.2bn EU fine payment (about negative USD 3.9bn excluding it). Quarterly capex reported USD 51.4bn, trailing-twelve-month capex USD 160bn.
Operating income rose 30% y/y. Search as a share of total revenue fell to 49.7% from 55.3%.
risk_factors: Search monetisation: AI answers and AI Mode earn less per query than traditional results, so growth in queries is not turning into revenue growth.
Disintermediation: commercial queries answered inside ChatGPT never reach Google's ad auction, and OpenAI now sells ads against them.
Cannibalisation: Google's own AI Overviews and AI Mode may reduce clicks on the click-based ad format that funds the company.

Cash flow and returns: capex of USD 160bn over twelve months, two straight quarters of negative free cash flow, and a mix shift from capital-light Search to capital-intensive Cloud lowers return on capital.
Advertiser budget reallocation to AI surfaces such as ChatGPT Ads.
Counter-risk to the threat thesis: ChatGPT Ads are small, performance is questioned, reporting is aggregate-only and the USD 2.5bn 2026 target is doubted by sceptics.

tension_points.bull_case: Google keeps about 90% of conventional searches, and query growth is the strongest in five years. Alphabet owns chips, cloud, models and distribution, so it can serve AI answers cheaply and capture AI demand whichever company wins the interface. Cloud revenue more than doubled to USD 30.7bn.
tension_points.bear_case: Search growth fell to 12% from 17-19% while queries grew faster, so revenue per query is falling. OpenAI now sells ads on commercial queries, and a few points of search budget moving would be material. Capex of USD 160bn and negative free cash flow lower returns as Cloud replaces Search profit.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further Search growth below the 17-19% range, or paid clicks falling relative to cost-per-click in the 10-Q, would confirm the bear case. The report names OpenAI's booked ad revenue and advertiser budget allocation as the other items to monitor.

theme_stances.key_argument: Q3 is the first quarter where the competitive narrative and the numbers line up, and the metric to watch is Search growth rather than market share.
theme_stances.evidence: Q3 is the first quarter where the competitive narrative and the numbers line up

theme_stances.key_argument: OpenAI does not need to win the auction outright to hurt Google's growth rate.
